sets.title: Invoice totals with no noise (control)
sets.description: The computeTotals method in three billing classes, all pristine. Carrier A, B, and C are all identical (no logging inserted). This is the control set for K-19: tools should detect all three as clones without any noise present.
sets.notes: Control set for K-19 (nz_logging). All three carriers are pristine — no logger->info noise. Detectors should find all three members with high confidence.

capability_probe.pass_criterion: Tool correctly pairs all 3 carriers despite presence of logger->info noise in probe set
capability_probe.fail_meaning: Tool cannot filter out logger->info noise; reports no pair or missed clone between noisy carriers

distractors.reason: near-miss: same invoice line-item vocabulary and foreach-over-items shape, but computes revenue/cost/margin instead of subtotal/tax/total — a different result

sets.title: Invoice totals with ONE logger->info noise insertion
sets.description: The computeTotals method in three billing classes. Carrier A is pristine; carrier B inserts a single $this->logger->info(...) call after the first statement (NZ-01, density 1); carrier C also inserts a logger call at a different position. This tests whether tools can filter out logging noise (NZ-01). Tools that cannot filter this noise will fail to pair B and C, or pair them incorrectly.
sets.notes: Probe set for K-19 (nz_logging). Uses NZ-01 (logging) transform to insert one $this->logger->info(...) call after the first statement in carrier B. Carrier C uses a different insertion position to create token variety. K-19 is the noise_filtering capability probe: tools must filter logger->info noise to correctly pair all three carriers.

capability_probe.pass_criterion: Tool correctly pairs all 3 carriers despite presence of logger->info noise in probe set
capability_probe.fail_meaning: Tool cannot filter out logger->info noise; reports no pair or missed clone between noisy carriers
